questions.q: What is metallic bonding?
a: The electrostatic attraction between positive metal ions and a sea of delocalized valence electrons
The sharing of electron pairs between non-metal atoms
The transfer of electrons from metals to non-metals
The weak intermolecular forces between neutral molecules

questions.q: Why are metals good conductors of electricity in both solid and liquid states?
a: Their delocalized outer shell electrons are free to move throughout the structure and carry an electrical current
They are made of polar molecules

questions.q: What term describes the ability of metals to be hammered or rolled into thin sheets without shattering?
What term describes the ability of metals to be drawn into long, thin wires?
Why are metals malleable and ductile rather than brittle like ionic crystals?
a: When a force is applied, layers of positive ions can slide over one another, and the delocalized electrons adjust to maintain strong attractions, preventing fracture
Because metal ions repel each other violently

questions.q: What is an alloy?
a: A pure element in liquid form
A mixture of a metal with one or more other elements (usually metals or carbon) designed to enhance specific properties

questions.q: Why are alloys typically stronger and harder than pure metals?
a: The different-sized atoms in an alloy distort the regular crystal lattice layers, preventing them from sliding over each other easily

questions.q: Which of the following is a well-known alloy of copper and tin?
What physical property causes metals to have a shiny appearance (luster) when freshly cut or polished?
a: Their delocalized electrons reflect light waves effectively

questions.q: Why do metals generally have high melting and boiling points?
a: They are made of light gases
A large amount of thermal energy is required to overcome the strong electrostatic attractions between the positive ions and the delocalized sea of electrons

questions.q: How do metals conduct thermal energy (heat) so efficiently?
a: Through the rapid movement and collision of delocalized electrons and vibrating positive ions that transfer kinetic energy quickly

questions.q: Which of the following metals is a liquid at room temperature?
What is brass composed of as an alloy?
What is steel primarily an alloy of?
a: Iron and a controlled amount of carbon (plus other metals)

questions.q: Why is pure copper often alloyed with zinc to make brass for musical instruments or plumbing fittings?
a: To make it softer and melt at lower temperatures
To increase its hardness, strength, and resistance to corrosion compared to pure copper
To make it dissolve in water

questions.q: What happens to the electrical conductivity of a metal when its temperature is increased significantly?
a: Conductivity decreases because vibrating metal ions impede the smooth flow of delocalized electrons

questions.q: Which of the following describes the structure of a solid metal?
a: A giant lattice of positive metal ions surrounded by a moving sea of delocalized valence electrons
A collection of separate neutral molecules held by weak forces
A 3D network of covalent bonds between non-metals
An alternating array of positive and negative ions

questions.q: Why are many structural bridges and buildings constructed using steel rather than pure iron?
a: Steel is much stronger, resists bending, and has better structural durability due to carbon additions
Pure iron is too expensive and heavy

questions.q: What is the origin of the 'delocalized electrons' in a metallic bond?
a: Electrons brought in from the air
Outer shell (valence) electrons that detach from metal atoms and roam freely throughout the lattice
Inner core electrons stripped by heat

questions.q: Which of the following metals is known for being extremely soft, reactive, and having a low density (capable of floating on oil)?
How does the number of delocalized electrons per atom typically affect the melting point and strength of a metal (e.g., comparing sodium with 1 valence electron to aluminum with 3)?
a: More delocalized electrons create stronger electrostatic attractions, resulting in higher melting points and greater hardness
More electrons make the metal softer and liquid at room temperature
Valence electrons have no effect on melting point
Metals with more electrons do not conduct electricity

questions.q: Which property of metals explains why they cannot be easily compressed?
a: The positive metal ions are packed closely together with very little empty space between them
They are made of hollow cages

questions.q: Why are aircraft bodies often constructed from aluminum alloys rather than pure aluminum or heavy steel?
a: Aluminum alloys combine high tensile strength and corrosion resistance with low density (light weight)
Aluminum alloys are cheaper than wood

questions.q: What term describes the ability of certain metal alloys (like nitinol) to return to their original shape after being deformed when heated?
Which of the following is a property shared by almost all metals except mercury?
a: Solid at room temperature with a crystalline structure

questions.q: How does adding atoms of a different size to form an alloy prevent layers of metal ions from sliding past each other easily?
a: Different-sized atoms disrupt the regular orderly rows of the lattice, acting as 'speed bumps' that block dislocation movement

questions.q: Which metal is widely used for electrical wiring in homes due to its excellent electrical conductivity and ductility, second only to silver?
What happens when a metal is struck by a hammer?
a: It shatters into sharp ionic shards like glass
It deforms without breaking because ion layers slide and delocalized electrons cushion the shift

questions.q: Why do transition metals generally have higher melting points and greater hardness than Group 1 alkali metals?
a: Transition metals contribute more electrons per atom to the delocalized electron sea, forming much stronger metallic bonds

questions.q: What is solder, an alloy commonly used in electronics to join electrical components together, typically made of?
Why are jewelry and wedding rings often made of 18-carat gold (an alloy of gold mixed with copper and silver) rather than 100% pure 24-carat gold?
a: Pure gold is too expensive to mine
Pure gold is too soft and easily scratched, so alloying it increases its durability and scratch resistance

questions.q: Which of the following phenomena occurs when metal surfaces react with oxygen and moisture in the environment over time?
What role do the positive metal ions play in holding a metallic structure together?
a: They attract the surrounding sea of delocalized electrons through strong electrostatic forces
They form covalent bonds with air

questions.q: Why is stainless steel (an alloy of iron, chromium, and nickel) resistant to rusting compared to pure iron?
a: Chromium forms a tough, invisible protective oxide layer on the surface that prevents oxygen and water from reaching the iron underneath

questions.q: Which of the following describes the electrical resistance of pure metals as temperature decreases toward absolute zero?
a: Resistance drops dramatically, and some metals become superconductors with zero electrical resistance

questions.q: Which of the following properties distinguishes metals from non-metals in solid form?
a: Thermal and electrical conductivity, malleability, and luster
